purpose: Load a portable agentic frontend design operating system as reusable Terra context for product-quality UI workflow authoring and execution.

sourceRefs.purpose: The project or organization frontend design orchestration source of truth. It can be supplied by hosted Terra context, run input, or a local context-source binding.
Optional local or organization folder containing reusable frontend design standards, prompts, templates, workflows, and memory.
Optional standards directory for frontend quality bars, visual rubrics, accessibility expectations, and anti-generic UI rules.
Optional role prompt directory for product strategy, design direction, implementation, critique, QA, and lessons recording.
Optional artifact template directory for briefs, handoffs, screenshot reports, critic reports, scorecards, and lessons.
Optional workflow playbook directory for single-surface, site-wide review, site-wide execution, critique, and final approval loops.
Optional local taste, rejected-pattern, successful-pattern, and lessons memory directory. This is operator-local by default and must not be required for hosted use.

setup.hostedUse: Hosted Terra deployments should serve the context pack and built-in workflow primitives without requiring the operator to clone the TerraForm repo. Optional project-specific context is supplied through run inputs, uploaded artifacts, or a generated context-source binding set.
setup.portabilityPolicy: Context packs must not contain machine-specific absolute paths. Concrete local paths belong only in non-production context-source binding files generated during setup.

fivePillarMapping.orchestratorUse: Load design standards, product framing, repo survey, brand assets, screenshots, prior lessons, and local workflow source material.
Select only the surface, brand, component, route, state, and evidence context needed by the active role.
Apply frontend rubric thresholds, defect taxonomy, critique gates, screenshot evidence, human taste approval, and final disposition.
Bind model, CLI, Playwright, patch, command, filesystem, and future browser-preview tools through explicit adapter bindings.
Preserve production UI copy quality, brand tone, concise operator updates, and clear role-specific output contracts.

authoringMethod: Survey the repo and target surface before visual direction.
Define page goal, primary action, user motivation, success proxy, and copy constraints.
Inspect brand identity, assets, routes, components, tokens, and state patterns.
Generate multiple thesis-distinct directions before implementation.
Capture selected direction and handoff before code changes.
Capture desktop and mobile screenshots before approval.
Critique with evidence, route defects to patch loops, and rescore after fixes.

Run deterministic artifact-quality validation before final approval so thin directions, weak handoffs, incomplete screenshots, permissive critics, partial scorecards, and unapproved taste decisions cannot pass.
nonNegotiables: Do not jump from vague product intent directly to code.
Do not skip repo survey, product framing, brand and asset inspection, selected direction, handoff, screenshots, critique, scorecard, or lessons.
Do not pass work that is merely not bad.
Do not pass work that looks good but fails the page goal.
Do not accept placeholder, filler, generic, unsupported, or off-tone visible copy.
Do not accept a high-level revamp or site-wide execution where requested pages only received a shared CSS layer, representative screenshots, or pending human taste approval.
Do not treat artifact existence or summary booleans as proof of frontend design quality; the artifact-quality report must inspect the real artifact contents.
Do not let second-opinion critique replace Codex as orchestrator or implementer.
Do not allow a design workflow to depend on one model, CLI, or machine-specific local path.
